  Councilmember Williams, Vice Mayor Madison)

  to discuss the following closed session item:

  Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(4) (one potential case)

  Agency Designated Representatives: Miguel Marquez and Tiffany
  Jacobs-Quinn
  Employee Organizations: Pasadena Police Officers Association
  (PPOA); Pasadena Police Lieutenants Association (PPLA)

  The above closed session items were discussed, with no reportable
  action at this time.

  On the order of the Mayor, the regular meeting reconvened at 6:21 p.m.
  The pledge of allegiance was led by Councilmember Hampton.

  CEREMONIAL MATTERS Mayor Gordo presented a proclamation declaring the month of April

L  2024 as Donate Life Month in the City of Pasadena and recognized the
  lives saved through organ donations. Alien Jolley, One Legacy
  Ambassador, accepted the proclamation on behalf of the organization
  and shared the story of his young daughter's organ donation.

  Council Minutes  1  04/08/2024
   Mayor Gordo presented a proclamation declaring April 11-17, 2024 as
  Black Maternal Health Week in the City of Pasadena, and reaffirmed
  the City's commitment to eliminate racial disparities in health outcomes.
  Stella Clingmon Simon, Maternal Child Health Program Manager, and
  Monette dark, Black Infant Health Program Coordinator, thanked the
  Mayor and City Council for the recognition and accepted the
  proclamation on behalf of the City's Health Department, and spoke on
  the Department's initiatives to address this nationwide crisis.

  Mayor Gordo presented a proclamation recognizing April 2024 as
  Sexual Assault Prevention and Awareness Month, and encouraged
  everyone to participate in Denim Day on April 24, 2024 by wearing
  jeans, as part of the international effort to communicate that there is
  never an invitation to rape. Vanessa Rodriguez, Vice Chair of the
  Commission on the Status of Women (CSW), and Leticia Lopez, CSW
  Staff, accepted the proclamation on behalf of the Commission, thanked
  the Council for the recognition, provided comments on the importance
  of addressing together the underlying issues of sexual assault as a
  community.

  Councilmember Hampton thanked the proclamation recipients for their
  hard work and requested that City staff take into further consideration
  these public safety and public health initiatives during the upcoming
  budget consideration.

  Mayor Gordo announced that the 710 Highway Ad Hoc Committee has
  been established and the meeting schedule has yet to be determined.
  He noted that the ad hoc committee members include himself, Vice
  Mayor Madison, Councilmember Hampton, and Councilmember Lyon.

  PUBLIC COMMENT ON  Nathan Lafontaine, Pasadena resident, expressed frustrations with
  MATTERS NOT ON THE  loud music in stores and how it affects his misophonia.
  AGENDA
  Heavenly Hughes, My Tribe Rise, spoke in recognition of April as
  Autism Awareness month, and thanked the proclamation recipients for
  their contributions to the community.

PUBLIC HEARINGS  APPROVAL OF RECOMMENDED SEWER USE FEE RATE
  STRUCTURE AND RATE ADJUSTMENTS (Public Works Dept.)
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1) Find that the proposed action is not a project as defined in the
  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Public Resources Code
  Section 21065, 21080(b)(8) and State CEQA Guidelines Sections
  15378(a) and (b)(4), and that even if it were a project, the proposed
  sewer use fee increases are statutorily exempt pursuant to Section
  15273 (Rates, Tolls, Fares, and Charges) under State CEQA
  Guidelines and as such, is not subject to environmental review;
  (2) Open a Public Hearing to receive public comment on the
  recommended adjustments to Sewer Use Fee rate structure and
  implement the Fiscal Year (FY) 2025 through FY 2029 rate adjustments
  effective July 1, 2024 or as soon as practicable thereafter;
  (3) Consider all protests against the proposed Sewer Use Fee rate
  increase in accordance with Proposition 218;
  (4) Following the close of the Public Hearing, approve the
  recommended Sewer Use Fee rate structure and rate adjustments; and
  (5) Direct the City Attorney to prepare an amendment to the Sewer
  Use Charge Ordinance (Ordinance) implementing the changes to the
  Sewer Use Fee rate structure and rates described in the agenda report.

  City Clerk Jomsky opened the public hearing and reported that the
  public hearing notice was mailed to all residents on February 21,2024.
  hie also reported that 1 letter in support of the staff recommendation
  and 290 letters protesting the proposed sewer rate structure and rate
  adjustments, and/or expressing concerns regarding the financial
  impacts that the increase would have on residents, were received by
  the City Clerk's Office, distributed to the City Council, posted online,
  and made part of the public record.

  Tony Olmos, Director of Public Works provided introductory remarks
  on the item, and introduced the consulting firm, Raftelis Financial
  Consultants, who assisted staff by preparing the proposed rate study.
  Director Olmos reported that the proposed increases are necessary
  due to expenditures exceeding revenues received from the current
  rates.

Council Minutes  10  04/08/2024
   Steve Gagnon, Raftelis Financial Consultant, presented a Powerpoint
  presentation on the comprehensive rate study; reported that the City
  has not raised sewer rates by more than CPI since 2007, noted that the
  sewer fund has a negative cash balance, and highlighted that capital
  improvement projects have been delayed in order to continue normal
  operations. Director Olmos reported on community outreach efforts and
  presented the combined impacts of the utility rate increases.

  The following individuals spoke in opposition to the proposed sewer
  rate structure and rate adjustments, and/or expressed concerns
  regarding the financial impacts that the proposed increases would have
  on residents:

  James Kirn, Pasadena resident
  Chris Patton, Pasadena resident
  Janice Stimson, Pasadena resident
  Richard Longobard, Pasadena resident
  Adrians Lim, representing Mountain Park Townhouse Villas HOA
  Eisa Saenz, Pasadena resident
  Peggy Names, Pasadena resident
  Rose Malmberg, Pasadena resident
  Kwok-Yin Cheng, Pasadena resident
  Joan Longoboard, Pasadena resident

  Councilmember Hampton emphasized that the proposed rate increase
  is extremely steep, agreed that the impacts would be difficult for
  residents, and advocated for more gradual rate increases spread over
  the years.

  In response to Councilmember Masuda's inquiry regarding why rates
  had not increased since 2007, Director Olmos stated that although CPI
  was previously sustainable with the previous rate, due to recent
  inflation impacts, the proposed increase is needed to keep up with
  current costs. Director Olmos reported that without the rate increase,
  the City would be unable to maintain sewage systems in compliance
  with legal requirements, which could create liabilities for the City. City
  Manager Marquez added that deferred maintenance would be more
  costly than proper/regular maintenance. In response to Councilmember
  Masuda's inquiry regarding imposing fees on developers, Director
  Olmos stated that a sewer facility fee is charged to developers based
  on the designs of the project and number affixtures being installed.

  Councilmember Lyon expressed agreement with the proposed rates,
  noting that despite the steepness of the increase, they are still well
  below rates of adjacent cities. He advocated for future built-in
  mechanisms (i.e., if reserves drop below a certain percentage) to
L  trigger conversations or rate studies for rate increases.

  In response to Councilmember Rivas' and Councilmember Jones'
  inquiries regarding alternative scenarios to the proposed rate

  Council Minutes  11  04/08/2024
   increases, Director Olmos noted that any lesser rate increase would
  change the outcome of the capital reserves over the next 5 years. He
  stated that if the proposed rate increase was halved, revenues would
  remain insufficient and capital projects would be continually deferred
  over the next few years, until revenues stabilize.

  Vice Mayor Madison noted that expenditures exceed revenues in the
  staff report and inquired what funds were utilized to cover the costs of
  these expenditures. Director Olmos stated that a balanced budget was
  maintained by not building certain capital projects. Vice Mayor Madison
  requested additional time to consider this issue, and asked that
  Pasadena Water and Power staff also be present when this matter is
  discussed in the future.

  Discussion ensued regarding the adopted budget allocation for the
  Fiscal Year (FY) 2024 sewer fund, the lack of a formal reserve policy,
  options/impacts if the City determined to raise revenues below the staff
  recommendation, and the resulting impacts on operating costs,
  capital/building reserves, and the availability of funds for sewer-related
  CIP projects.

  Kris Markarian, Deputy Director of Public Works, provided clarification
  on the identified CIP projects, the current appropriations, and what
  Council has adopted as part of the CIP budget process. She noted the
  5-year CIP budget and project list is adopted each year, so the
  appropriations and projects change each year.

  Vice Mayor Madison spoke on what appears to be a budget shortfall,
  questioned how staff made adjustments (specifically if City Council
  authorization was provided), and requested that City staff to bring back
  additional information and details to address these questions.

  Discussion ensued regarding the movement of funds from the
  operational budget to the CIP budget, and the adopted FY 2024-28 CIP
  budget and projects presented by staff. The City Council directed City
  staff to provide a revised report on the capital improvement budget
  details, with consistent terminology, to assist the City Council in
  understanding how funds were utilized.

  City Manager Marquez suggested that the public hearings on Sewer
  Use Rate Adjustment and Refuse Rate Adjustment be continued and
  moved to May 6, 2024 at 5:30 p.m.

  increases, (2) the three fund buckets of operational costs, capital
  improvement budget/investments, and reserve funds; and (3) include
  Pasadena Water & Power staff and Finance staff to be present at the
